items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: I used to go up there quite often with Fats Waller.

ctx.x: They always hired a piano player and probably a singer. The singer usually up there was a girl by the name of Betty Treadwell that used to sing up there and the piano player usually -- the regular was Sylvester Scott, who was another one of the old-timers from around town here now and he was one of the regular piano players. But, by the same token, we used to come in after we got off at three o'clock in the morning and bring guys like Fats Waller and he would sit in and all you had to do was keep two or three…
for a long time and have a good time. I used to go up there quite often with Fats Waller.

Then they had other good guys that would come in and play a tune or so at a time like Nat King Cole. He was a wonderful pianist, as well as being a singer. He was one of the best pianists there was in the world. He used to come up and later, on the tail end, Erroll may have gotten into it, although I'm not sure because Erroll didn't get out into the California scene -- Erroll Garner, I'm speaking of -- until after World War II.
